- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model may overestimate mean reversion; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price action (last 7–10 days); apply a 2–5% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast to align with observed momentum.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting; add 1–2 days of early upward momentum to forecast to capture sentiment shift.
